September 25, 2026
Media Opps: Bloomberg, Poynter, The Boston Globe
A Local Investigations Fellowship with a salary of $85,000
Webinar Panel: Journalism and AI:
Addressing Fears, Anxieties, and Concerns
Wednesday, October 28, 2026
10:00 AM PT / 1:00 PM ET
Free to attend
In this webinar panel, three seasoned journalists —
Taylor Lorenz
,
Alexandra Marvar
, and
Brian Merchant
— will share how media workers can navigate AI tools and the various ways in which this technology has transformed the industry.
This panel will touch upon how legacy media outlets are coming up with AI rules, and what writers can do to protect their work. In addition, the panelists will discuss larger questions about how AI has changed the industry: Is it possible to integrate these tools in a workflow without plagiarizing other writers' work? Is there a double standard of media outlets banning freelancers from using these tools, while editors use in-house AI tools? What does it mean to have original prose in a time when LLMs can mimic style?
Register
here
.
ICYMI: Interview with Bridget Read
On the latest podcast
episode
, Bridget Read, a features writer at
New York Magazine
, gave listeners a behind-the-scenes look on how she researches and reports her longform journalism.
How to Write a Zeitgeisty Feature ft. Bridget Read
Podcast Episode · The Study Hall Podcast · September 22 · 41m
Apple Podcasts
The listings are now posted throughout the week on our
Opportunity Finder
.
If you have any technical questions or want to submit an opportunity m, please email ‘
support AT studyhall DOT xyz
with “Opps:” in the subject line.
Please note:
Anything marked as “
NEW
” is from the past seven days and is included alongside newly added opps (but more than one week old). Finally, old opps from previous issues with upcoming deadlines are listed at the end of the newsletter.
STUDY HALL COURSES:
Reporting On Politics 101
Reporting on local and national politics can feel opaque to those who have yet to crack the code. Perhaps more than even culture writing, politics requires knowledge of a specific, technical kind of language. In this
class
, Grace Byron will guide you on how to generate ideas, find outlets, and use the lingo that veteran politics reporters and editors use when building a story. From interviewing subjects, write-arounds, and opinion pieces, you will analyze a few pitches and stories to get a better sense of how to get started. You'll leave this one-hour class feeling prepared to start your political reporting journey and hopefully have a few ideas of how to get tips and pitch new editors.
Grace’s work has appeared in
The New Yorker,
Vogue
, and
The Nation
.
The 1.5 hour course will take place September 28th 10 AM PDT.
The standard price is $99. Study Hall members can use the discount code “
studyhallmember
” to bring the price to $49.50. For any questions, email
support@studyhall.xyz
.
Sign up
.
OTHER RESOURCES
▶ Add to the Rate-Sharing Database
The
Freelance Solidarity Project
maintains an ongoing
Rate Sharing Database
to build a clearer picture of freelance pay—and, ultimately, change how we are paid. Add your rates, and help build a more equitable future for freelancers in the industry.
The Institute for Independent Journalists have opened registration for the
Fall 2026 Business of Freelancing course
, offered from Oct. 1 through Nov. 19.
This eight-week, live online course provides a comprehensive foundation in the business of freelance journalism and has sold out every time they’ve presented it. Each session combines real-world strategy with personalized guidance, covering topics such as rate setting, time and income management, client relationships, and long-term planning.
Registration is $249 before Sept 24, and $299 after.
They’ve also announced
their lineup of webinars
for freelancers, featuring assigning editors, fellowship directors, and independent creators. Each webinar runs from 12-1:15 pm EST and costs $30.
Sept. 25 Dig In: How to Succeed on the Food Beat
Oct. 16 Global Freelancing: The Secrets of Traveling Entrepreneurs
Nov. 20 Fund your Freelancing with Fellowships and Grants
Dec. 11 Pitching Arts, Culture, and Travel Stories
Jan. 22 Winning Revenue Strategies for Creator Journalists
Feb. 4-5 Pitch the Editors: Sign Up for 1:1 Pitch Sessions

Please note:
We are not endorsing every publication or company listed here. Engaging with a publication or company is entirely up to the reader. We currently sort each section from the most to least recently posted.
Final note:
Before pitching,
always
check the links to confirm the opportunities are still available.

Candidates should have at least five years of professional journalism experience reporting on legal, governmental, or regulatory affairs at a national or regional level, a demonstrated track record of reporting on deadline, and the ability to manage multiple stories under shifting deadlines.
